section_summary: This section (pages 81–160) documents State Department and military processing of travel clearances, entry permits, and commercial entry applications for occupied Japan during December 1949. It covers diverse individual cases involving foreign merchants, business representatives, and dependents seeking entry to revive international trade in textiles, scrap metal, and consumer goods under SCAP regulations. The materials also record policy discussions on liberalizing foreign travel for Japanese technicians, as well as formal appeals and legal petitions concerning the postwar forced repatriation and property confiscation of German civilians.

subfiles.about: Appeals and legal brief against the forced repatriation and property confiscation of over two thousand German residents from Japan.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew / Johannes Barth / Japan Committee of the East Asiatic Association
subfiles.summary: Former Ambassador Joseph C. Grew forwards an appeal from long-time Japan resident Johannes Barth and a detailed legal petition from the Japan Committee of the East Asiatic Association in Hamburg. The documents protest the postwar forced repatriation of approximately 2,200 German civilians from Japan and the seizure and auctioning of their private property by SCAP occupation authorities, arguing these actions violated international law and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
